title: Finish before starting more
hook: Three started tasks are not three finished tasks.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Compare serial completion to round-robin partial progress.

objective: Compare serial completion to round-robin partial progress.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Three started tasks are not three finished tasks. Which completes the first five-minute job at minute five? Correct option: One job to completion. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The bars represent whole-task execution. Starting everything would spread progress without completing the first job; completion and activity are different counts.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: order. Exercise only; no measured productivity gain. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, work-in-process-limit fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. Stage rules: cumulative execution with stated setup cost; waiting is sum of start times; late means finish>due; dependency breach means predecessor is later in order. For the initial schedule, every unfinished task receives one five-minute slice per round; displayed rectangles are actual execution slices. First completion is min of completion times. The alternate schedule runs whole jobs serially. No switching overhead or empirical efficiency is assumed.
